stemBlocks.value: Part (ii) of question 8 on this page: the trapezium A on the square grid has vertices (-5, 4), (-4, 4), (-3, 2) and (-5, 2). Draw the image of A after a translation by the vector (4, -7) and label this image A".
Think first: A translation moves every vertex by the same amount, so add 4 to each x and subtract 7 from each y.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p261-q02 from workbook page 261.

solutionSteps.instruction: Read the vertices of trapezium A from the grid.

contentBlocks.value: The trapezium sits between x = -5 and x = -3, y = 2 and y = 4.

solutionSteps.instruction: State the translation rule from the vector: 4 units right and 7 units down.

contentBlocks.value: The top number moves you along x, the bottom number along y.

solutionSteps.instruction: Apply the rule to each vertex.
Plot the image points and join them in the same order to draw A".

contentBlocks.value: A" is congruent to A and the same way up, just shifted.
Result: Trapezium A" drawn below the x-axis

strategyBlocks.value: Read the vertices of A, apply (x, y) -> (x + 4, y - 7) to each one, then plot the four images and join them in the same order.

whyThisWorks.value: A translation is described by a single displacement vector that applies to every point of the shape, so the figure keeps its size, shape and orientation and only its position changes. Adding the vector's components to the coordinates of each vertex is exactly the same as sliding the whole figure along that displacement.

commonErrors.misconception: Reading the vector as 4 up and 7 right instead of 4 right and 7 down.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Reading the vector as 4 up and 7 right instead of 4 right and 7 down.

commonErrors.misconception: Adding 7 instead of subtracting it because the negative sign is missed.

commonErrors.misconception: Translating only one vertex and then drawing the shape by eye.

examTip.value: Translate the vertex nearest the origin first and check it by counting squares on the grid; if that one is right, the rest follow from the same arithmetic.
